input.strategy_title: Adopt structured JSON logging across RHOAI components
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

RHOAI components log in inconsistent formats — plain text, key=value, and
ad-hoc JSON — which breaks centralized log queries and makes support cases
expensive: correlating one user request across Dashboard, serving, and
pipelines requires per-component parsing rules. The platform needs one
structured logging convention, and each component needs to adopt it. Component
adoptions are independent of each other once the convention exists.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1  | P0 | A platform logging convention is published: JSON schema, required fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id), and library guidance per language (Go, Python, TypeScript). |
| HLR-2  | P0 | Dashboard emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-3  | P0 | KServe controller and serving runtimes emit convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-4  | P1 | Data Science Pipelines (operator and API server) emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-5  | P1 | Model Registry emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-6  | P1 | TrustyAI services emit convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-7  | P1 | Notebooks (notebook-controller) emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-8  | P2 | Training Operator emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-9  | P2 | Documentation describes the log format and example queries for common support scenarios. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- KServe
- Data Science Pipelines
- Model Registry
- TrustyAI
- Notebooks
- Training Operator

## Out of Scope

- Log storage, retention, or forwarding infrastructure
- Metrics and tracing conventions (logging only)

## Open Questions

None — the convention work (HLR-1) is prerequisite design, and per-component
adoptions are mechanical once it lands.

# Publish platform structured logging convention

## Description

This epic delivers the platform-wide structured logging convention that all
RHOAI components will adopt: a published JSON log schema, the set of required
fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id), and library
guidance for each of the platform's implementation languages (Go, Python,
TypeScript). It is the prerequisite design deliverable for every component
adoption in this strategy — component adoptions are mechanical once it lands.

## Scope

- Define the JSON schema for the structured log format, including the required
  fields: timestamp, level, component, namespace, and correlation id.
- Define how optional/additional fields are carried without breaking schema
  conformance.
- Publish library guidance per language for Go, Python, and TypeScript:
  recommended logging library and how to emit convention-conformant records
  with it, including propagation of the correlation id.
- Publish the convention at a location accessible to all adopting component
  teams.
- Socialize the convention with the adopting component teams so adoption can
  proceed (review of the draft, not per-component implementation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A JSON schema for the log format is published and validates example records
  from each of Go, Python, and TypeScript.
- Every record conforming to the schema carries the required fields:
  timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id.
- Library guidance exists for Go, Python, and TypeScript, each demonstrating
  emission of a schema-conformant record.
- The convention document is published and reachable by all adopting component
  teams.
- The convention has been reviewed by representatives of the adopting
  component teams with no unresolved objections to the required-field set.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A platform logging convention is published: JSON schema,
  required fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id),
  and library guidance per language (Go, Python, TypeScript).

# Dashboard emits convention-conformant structured logs

## Description

This epic migrates the Dashboard (odh-dashboard) to the platform structured
logging convention: its log output becomes valid JSON conforming to the
published schema, carrying the required fields (timestamp, level, component,
namespace, correlation id) and following the TypeScript library guidance. This
is one of the P0 adoptions that make a single user request correlatable across
Dashboard, serving, and pipelines without per-component parsing rules.

## Scope

- Adopt the recommended TypeScript logging library per the convention's
  library guidance in the Dashboard codebase.
- Convert existing Dashboard log statements to emit convention-conformant
  JSON records with the required fields, including correlation id propagation
  for a user request where the Dashboard is the entry point.
- Retain the diagnostic information currently carried by existing log
  statements (no loss of message content during migration).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dashboard log output is valid JSON that validates against the published
  convention schema.
- Emitted records carry the required fields: timestamp, level, component,
  namespace, correlation id.
- Existing diagnostic messages remain available in the structured output
  (spot-check per migrated log area).
- Dashboard CI/build is green with the migrated logging.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Dashboard emits convention-conformant logs.
